Danube.question: Since the Rhine flows north towards the _____, a continental divide beginning at Piz Lunghin divides large parts of southern Germany, which is sometimes referred to as the European Watershed
Danube.fact: Today the Commission include riparian and non-riparian states.  == Geology == Although the headwaters of the Danube are relatively small today, geologically, the Danube is much older than the Rhine, with which its catchment area competes in today's southern Germany.  This has a few interesting geological complications.  Since the Rhine flows north towards the North Sea, a continental divide beginning at Piz Lunghin divides large parts of southern Germany, which is sometimes referred to as the European Watershed.  Before the last ice age in the Pleistocene, the Rhine started at the southwestern tip of the Black Forest, while the waters from the Alps that today feed the Rhine were carried east by the so-called Urdonau (original Danube).  Parts of this ancient river's bed, which was much larger than today's Danube, can still be seen in (now waterless) canyons in today's landscape of the Swabian Alb.  The erosion of the Upper Rhine valley led to stream capture; waters from the Alps changed their direction and began feeding the Rhine

Danube.question: Most of this water resurfaces only _____ (7
Danube.fact: Today's upper Danube is thus an underfit stream.  Since the Swabian Alb is largely shaped of porous limestone, and since the Rhine's level is much lower than the Danube's, today subsurface rivers carry much water from the Danube to the Rhine.  On many days in the summer, when the Danube carries little water, it completely sinks into these underground channels at two locations in the Swabian Alb, which are referred to as the Donauversickerung (Danube Sink).  Most of this water resurfaces only 12 km (7. 5 mi) south at the Aachtopf, Germany's wellspring with the highest flow, an average of 8,500 L/s (300 cu ft/s), north of Lake Constance—thus feeding the Rhine.  The European Water Divide applies only for those waters that pass beyond this point, which only occurs during the days of the year when the Danube carries enough water to survive the sinkholes in the Donauversickerung.  Since such large volumes of underground water erode much of the surrounding limestone, it is predicted that the Danube upper course will one day disappear entirely in favor of the Rhine, an event called stream capturing

Danube.question: From 37 CE to the reign of the _____ I (364–375) the Danubian Limes was the northeastern border of the Empire, with occasional interruptions such as the fall of the Danubian Limes in 259
Danube.fact: Alexander the Great defeated the Triballian king Syrmus and the northern barbarian Thracian and Illyrian tribes by advancing from Macedonia as far as the Danube in 336 BCE.  Under the Romans, the Danube formed the border of the Empire with the tribes to the north almost from its source to its mouth.  At the same time, it was a route for the transport of troops and the supply of settlements downstream.  From 37 CE to the reign of the Emperor Valentinian I (364–375) the Danubian Limes was the northeastern border of the Empire, with occasional interruptions such as the fall of the Danubian Limes in 259.  The crossing of the Danube into Dacia was achieved by the Imperium Romanum, first in two battles in 102 and then in 106 after the construction of a bridge in 101 near the garrison town of Drobeta at the Iron Gate.  This victory over Dacia under Decebalus enabled the Province of Dacia to be created, but in 271 it was abandoned by emperor Aurelian.  Avars used the river as their southeastern border in the 6th century

Danube.fact: Proposals to build a number of new locks to improve navigation have not progressed, due in part to environmental concerns.  Downstream from the Freudenau locks in Vienna, canalization of the Danube was limited to the Gabčíkovo dam and locks near Bratislava and the two double Iron Gate locks in the border stretch of the Danube between Serbia and Romania.  These locks have larger dimensions.  Downstream of the Iron Gate, the river is free flowing all the way to the Black Sea, a distance of more than 860 kilometres (530 mi).  The Danube connects with the Rhine–Main–Danube Canal at Kelheim, with the Donaukanal in Vienna, and with the Danube–Black Sea Canal at Cernavodă.  Apart from a couple of secondary navigable branches, the only major navigable rivers linked to the Danube are the Drava, Sava and Tisa. Danube.fact: While traveling on the mainland was quite exhausting, most people preferred to travel by ship on the Danube. The route got its name from the Holy Roman Emperor Frederick I of Barbarossa and the crusaders as well as from Richard I of England who had been jailed in the Dürnstein Castle, which is situated above the Danube.  The most imperial journeys throughout time were those of the Habsburg family.  Once crowned in Frankfurt, the emperors ruled from Vienna and also held in Regensburg the Perpetual Diet of Regensburg. Desert.question: Small ripples form on the sand sheet when the wind exceeds _____/h (15 mph)
Desert.fact: A sand sheet is a near-level, firm expanse of partially consolidated particles in a layer that varies from a few centimeters to a few meters thick.  The structure of the sheet consists of thin horizontal layers of coarse silt and very fine to medium grain sand, separated by layers of coarse sand and pea-gravel which are a single grain thick.  These larger particles anchor the other particles in place and may also be packed together on the surface so as to form a miniature desert pavement.  Small ripples form on the sand sheet when the wind exceeds 24 km/h (15 mph).  They form perpendicular to the wind direction and gradually move across the surface as the wind continues to blow.  The distance between their crests corresponds to the average length of jumps made by particles during saltation.  The ripples are ephemeral and a change in wind direction causes them to reorganise

Desert.fact: Some are deciduous, shedding their leaves in the driest season, and others curl their leaves up to reduce transpiration. Desert plants maximize water uptake by having shallow roots that spread widely, or by developing long taproots that reach down to deep rock strata for ground water. Desert.fact: Herbivorous mammals obtain moisture from the plants they eat.  Species such as the addax antelope, dik-dik, Grant's gazelle and oryx are so efficient at doing this that they apparently never need to drink.  The camel is a superb example of a mammal adapted to desert life.  It minimizes its water loss by producing concentrated urine and dry dung, and is able to lose 40% of its body weight through water loss without dying of dehydration.  Carnivores can obtain much of their water needs from the body fluids of their prey.  Many other hot desert animals are nocturnal, seeking out shade during the day or dwelling underground in burrows. Reptiles cannot survive at this temperature and lizards will be prostrated by heat at 45 °C (113 °F).  They have few adaptations to desert life and are unable to cool themselves by sweating so they shelter during the heat of the day. Diomedes.fact: Tydeus was Athena's favorite warrior at the time, and when he was dying she wanted to offer him immortality (which she had obtained from her father).

Diomedes.fact: Diomedes' father, Tydeus, was among those who had been slain. Tydeus was Athena's favorite warrior at the time, and when he was dying she wanted to offer him immortality (which she had obtained from her father).

Diomedes.fact: Ten years later (according to Apollodorus) , the Epigoni set out to launch another expedition against Thebes, appointing Alcmaeon as their commander-in-chief.

Diomedes.fact: The main battle took place at Glisas where prince Aegialeus (son of Adrastus and heir to the throne) was slain by King Laodamas, who was in turn killed by Alcmaeon.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: With their king dead, the _____, believing this to be the end for them, sought counsel from the seer Tiresias, who urged them to flee the city
Diomedes.fact: With their king dead, the Thebans, believing this to be the end for them, sought counsel from the seer Tiresias, who urged them to flee the city.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: They did so, and, faced with no opposition, the _____ entered the city, plundering its treasures and tearing down its great walls
Diomedes.fact: They did so, and, faced with no opposition, the Epigoni entered the city, plundering its treasures and tearing down its great walls. Having achieved their objective, the Epigoni returned home, but not before they installed Thersander, son of the fallen prince Polynices (the instigator of the first Theban expedition), as the city's new ruler.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He was assassinated on the way (in _____) by Thersites and Onchestus
Diomedes.fact: He was assassinated on the way (in Arcadia) by Thersites and Onchestus.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography

Diomedes.fact: Both Sthenelus and Euryalus (former Epigoni) fought under his command with their armies.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He was overwhelming _____ in an armed sparring contest when the watching Achaeans bade the men to stop and take equal prizes because they feared for Ajax's life
Diomedes.fact: He was overwhelming Telamonian Ajax in an armed sparring contest when the watching Achaeans bade the men to stop and take equal prizes because they feared for Ajax's life.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He once vanquished _____ — the second best of the Trojan warriors — and could have struck him down
Diomedes.fact: He once vanquished Aeneas — the second best of the Trojan warriors — and could have struck him down.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He and _____ were the only Achaean heroes who participated in covert military operations that demanded discipline, bravery, courage, cunning, and resourcefulness
Diomedes.fact: He and Odysseus were the only Achaean heroes who participated in covert military operations that demanded discipline, bravery, courage, cunning, and resourcefulness.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He was the favorite warrior of _____ (who even drove his chariot once)
Diomedes.fact: He was the favorite warrior of Athena (who even drove his chariot once).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He was also the only hero except _____, son of Zeus, that attacked Olympian gods
Diomedes.fact: He was also the only hero except Heracles, son of Zeus, that attacked Olympian gods.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He even wounded _____, whom he struck with his spear
Diomedes.fact: He even wounded Ares, whom he struck with his spear.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He was the only _____ warrior apart from Achilles who carried such an arsenal of gear made by Hera's son
Diomedes.fact: He was the only Achaean warrior apart from Achilles who carried such an arsenal of gear made by Hera's son.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: It was created by a mortal smith but was blessed by _____, who gave it to Tydeus
Diomedes.fact: It was created by a mortal smith but was blessed by Athena, who gave it to Tydeus. Both of them were favorite heroes of Athena and each shared characteristics of their patron goddess – Odysseus her wisdom and cunning, and Diomedes her courage and skill in battle; though neither was wholly bereft of either aspect.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: They began to combine their efforts and actions already when being in _____
Diomedes.fact: They began to combine their efforts and actions already when being in Aulis. When the sacrifice of Iphigenia (Agamemnon's daughter) became a necessity for the Achaeans to sail away from Aulis, King Agamemnon had to choose between sacrificing his daughter and resigning from his post of high commander among Achaeans.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: When he decided to sacrifice his daughter to _____, Odysseus carried out this order of Agamemnon by luring Iphigenia from Mycenae to Aulis, where murder, disguised as wedding, awaited her
Diomedes.fact: When he decided to sacrifice his daughter to Artemis, Odysseus carried out this order of Agamemnon by luring Iphigenia from Mycenae to Aulis, where murder, disguised as wedding, awaited her.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: However, Pseudo-_____ has Agamemnon send Odysseus and Talthybius instead
Diomedes.fact: However, Pseudo-Apollodorus has Agamemnon send Odysseus and Talthybius instead.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: According to _____, neither of the two went to fetch Iphigenia, though he calls the plan Odysseus' idea in Iphigenia at Tauris
Diomedes.fact: According to Euripides, neither of the two went to fetch Iphigenia, though he calls the plan Odysseus' idea in Iphigenia at Tauris.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Another version says that he conspired with _____ against Palamedes, and under the pretence of having discovered a hidden treasure, they let him down into a well and there stoned him to death
Diomedes.fact: According to Euripides, neither of the two went to fetch Iphigenia, though he calls the plan Odysseus' idea in Iphigenia at Tauris. According to other stories, when Palamedes advised the Achaeans to return home, Odysseus accused him of being a traitor and forged false evidence and found a fake witness to testify against him, whereupon Palamedes was stoned to death.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: However, he still displays self-restraint and humility to retreat before Ares and give way to _____ thus remaining within mortal limits
Diomedes.fact: However, he still displays self-restraint and humility to retreat before Ares and give way to Apollo thus remaining within mortal limits. This is in contrast to Patroclus (who does not give way when opposed by Apollo) and Achilles (who resorts to fight the river Scamander on his own).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: This is in contrast to _____ (who does not give way when opposed by Apollo) and Achilles (who resorts to fight the river Scamander on his own)
Diomedes.fact: This is in contrast to Patroclus (who does not give way when opposed by Apollo) and Achilles (who resorts to fight the river Scamander on his own).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: However, when _____ earlier uses the same kind of taunting on Odysseus, he responds with anger
Diomedes.fact: Instances of Diomedes' maturity and intelligence as described in parts of the epic: In Book IV Agamemnon taunts Diomedes by calling him a far inferior fighter compared to his father. His enraged comrade Sthenelus urges Diomedes to stand up to Agamemnon by responding that he has bested his father and avenged his death by conquering Thebes.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: In Book IX, _____ proposes going back to Hellas because Zeus has turned against them
Diomedes.fact: His enraged comrade Sthenelus urges Diomedes to stand up to Agamemnon by responding that he has bested his father and avenged his death by conquering Thebes. Diomedes responded that it was part of Agamemnon's tasks as a leader to urge forward the Achaean soldiers, and that men of valour should have no problem withstanding such insults.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Fate and gods were with _____ at the start and therefore Zeus' interventions could be only temporary
Diomedes.fact: Fate and gods were with Achaeans at the start and therefore Zeus' interventions could be only temporary. Even if all other Achaeans lost their faith and went home, he and Sthenelus would still remain and continue to fight till Troy was sacked.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Even if all other _____ lost their faith and went home, he and Sthenelus would still remain and continue to fight till Troy was sacked
Diomedes.fact: Fate and gods were with Achaeans at the start and therefore Zeus' interventions could be only temporary. Even if all other Achaeans lost their faith and went home, he and Sthenelus would still remain and continue to fight till Troy was sacked.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: They had to return empty handed; _____ had told them that he will leave Troy and never return
Diomedes.fact: You are still young—you might be the youngest of my own children—still you have spoken wisely and have counselled the chief of the Achaeans not without discretion;'" Achaean council – Book IX When Agamemnon tried to appease Achilles's wrath so that he would fight again, by offering him many gifts, Nestor appointed three envoys to meet Achilles (Book IX). They had to return empty handed; Achilles had told them that he will leave Troy and never return.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: She responds by offering him a special vision to distinguish gods from men and asks him to wound _____ if she ever comes to battle
Diomedes.fact: She responds by offering him a special vision to distinguish gods from men and asks him to wound Aphrodite if she ever comes to battle.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He continues to make havoc among the _____ by killing Astynous, Hypeiron, Abas, Polyidus, Xanthus, Thoon, Echemmon and Chromius (two sons of Priam)
Diomedes.fact: He continues to make havoc among the Trojans by killing Astynous, Hypeiron, Abas, Polyidus, Xanthus, Thoon, Echemmon and Chromius (two sons of Priam).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Although he can face both of these warriors together, he knows that _____ may try to save her son, Aeneas
Diomedes.fact: Although he can face both of these warriors together, he knows that Aphrodite may try to save her son, Aeneas.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He also knows the history of _____' two horses (they descend from immortal steeds that Zeus had once given King Tros, original founder of Troy)
Diomedes.fact: Although he can face both of these warriors together, he knows that Aphrodite may try to save her son, Aeneas. He also knows the history of Aeneas' two horses (they descend from immortal steeds that Zeus had once given King Tros, original founder of Troy).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Since he has to carry out _____'s order, he orders Sthenelus to steal the horses while he faces Aeneas
Diomedes.fact: Since he has to carry out Athena's order, he orders Sthenelus to steal the horses while he faces Aeneas.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: They are taken by _____ to the Greek ships
Diomedes.fact: They are taken by Deipylus to the Greek ships.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Apollo comes to the rescue of Aeneas and sends the wounded _____ fleeing back to Olympus
Diomedes.fact: Aphrodite drops Aeneas while under attack by Diomedes, who is following Athena's orders. Apollo comes to the rescue of Aeneas and sends the wounded Aphrodite fleeing back to Olympus.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: The latter reminded her of mighty _____ (now, an Olympian himself) who held the record of wounding not one but two Olympians as a human
Diomedes.fact: The latter reminded her of mighty Heracles (now, an Olympian himself) who held the record of wounding not one but two Olympians as a human.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Urged by _____, Ares came to the battlefield to help Trojans
Diomedes.fact: Diomedes' transgression of attacking Apollo had its consequences. Urged by Apollo, Ares came to the battlefield to help Trojans.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Hera saw the havoc created by her son and together with Athena, she came to the _____' aid
Diomedes.fact: Identifying the god of war, Diomedes protected the Achaeans by ordering them to withdraw towards their ships. Hera saw the havoc created by her son and together with Athena, she came to the Achaeans' aid.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: I am following your instructions and retreating for I know that Ares is fighting among the _____"
Diomedes.fact: I am following your instructions and retreating for I know that Ares is fighting among the Trojans".

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: She also put on the helmet of _____, making her invisible to even gods
Diomedes.fact: She also put on the helmet of Hades, making her invisible to even gods.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: According to the instructions of _____, Priam's wife gathered matrons at the temple of Athena in the acropolis and offered the goddess the largest, fairest robe of Troy
Diomedes.fact: Hector's brother Helenus described Diomedes' fighting skills in this manner: "He fights with fury and fills men's souls with panic. I hold him mightiest of them all; we did not fear even their great champion Achilles, son of an immortal though he be, as we do this man: his rage is beyond all bounds, and there is none can vie with him in prowess." Helenus then sent Hector to the city of Troy to tell their mother about what was happening.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Meanwhile, one brave _____ named Glaucus challenged the son of Tydeus to a single combat
Diomedes.fact: Meanwhile, one brave Trojan named Glaucus challenged the son of Tydeus to a single combat.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: The phrase '_____ swap' originated from this incident
Diomedes.fact: The phrase 'Diomedian swap' originated from this incident.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: When they cast lots to choose one among those warriors, the Achaeans prayed "_____, grant that the lot fall on Ajax, or on the son of Tydeus, or upon Agamemnon." Ajax was chosen to fight Hector
Diomedes.fact: When they cast lots to choose one among those warriors, the Achaeans prayed "Father Zeus, grant that the lot fall on Ajax, or on the son of Tydeus, or upon Agamemnon." Ajax was chosen to fight Hector.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Idaeus of the _____ came for a peace negotiation, and he offered to give back all the treasures Paris stole plus more—everything except Helen
Diomedes.fact: Idaeus of the Trojans came for a peace negotiation, and he offered to give back all the treasures Paris stole plus more—everything except Helen. He made the Trojans stronger so they could drive away the Achaeans from battle.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography

Diomedes.fact: Idaeus of the Trojans came for a peace negotiation, and he offered to give back all the treasures Paris stole plus more—everything except Helen. He made the Trojans stronger so they could drive away the Achaeans from battle.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Seeing this, all the great _____ warriors—including the two Ajaxes, Agamemnon, Idomeneus and Odysseus—took flight

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Nestor could not escape because one of his horses was wounded by _____' arrow
Diomedes.fact: Nestor could not escape because one of his horses was wounded by Paris' arrow.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Seeing that _____'s life was in danger, the son of Tydeus shouted for Odysseus' help
Diomedes.fact: Nestor could not escape because one of his horses was wounded by Paris' arrow. Seeing that Nestor's life was in danger, the son of Tydeus shouted for Odysseus' help.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Struck by his spear, _____'s driver Eniopeus was slain
Diomedes.fact: Having Nestor as the driver, Diomedes bravely rushed towards Hector. Struck by his spear, Hector's driver Eniopeus was slain.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Taking a new driver, _____, Hector advanced forward again
Diomedes.fact: Taking a new driver, Archeptolemus, Hector advanced forward again. Zeus saw that both Hector and Archeptolemus were about to be slain by Diomedes and decided to intervene.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: When all the _____ seemed discouraged, Zeus sent an eagle as a good omen
Diomedes.fact: When all the Achaean seemed discouraged, Zeus sent an eagle as a good omen.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: I shall then know whether brave _____ will drive me back from the ships to the wall, or whether I shall myself slay him and carry off his bloodstained spoils
Diomedes.fact: Diomedes was the first warrior to read this omen, and he immediately attacked the Trojans and killed Agelaus. I shall then know whether brave Diomed will drive me back from the ships to the wall, or whether I shall myself slay him and carry off his bloodstained spoils.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: This speech signifies the nature of _____ tradition where fate and divine interventions have superiority over human choices
Diomedes.fact: This speech signifies the nature of Homeric tradition where fate and divine interventions have superiority over human choices.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Nestor believed in the importance of human choices and proposed to change _____' mind by offering many gifts
Diomedes.fact: Nestor believed in the importance of human choices and proposed to change Achilles' mind by offering many gifts. The embassy failed because Achilles himself had more faith in his own choices than fate or divine interventions.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: The embassy failed because _____ himself had more faith in his own choices than fate or divine interventions
Diomedes.fact: Nestor believed in the importance of human choices and proposed to change Achilles' mind by offering many gifts. The embassy failed because Achilles himself had more faith in his own choices than fate or divine interventions.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: This proposal was approved by both _____ and Odysseus
Diomedes.fact: He then criticized Diomedes for not making any positive proposal to replace Agamemnon's opinion – a failure which Nestor ascribed to his youth. This proposal was approved by both Agamemnon and Odysseus.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He threatened to leave _____, never to return believing that this choice will enable him to live a long life
Diomedes.fact: He threatened to leave Troy, never to return believing that this choice will enable him to live a long life. When the envoys returned, Diomedes criticized Nestor's decision and Achilles' pride saying that Achilles' personal choice of leaving Troy is of no importance (therefore, trying to change it with gifts is useless).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: During the _____ council held, Agamemnon asked for a volunteer to spy on the Trojans
Diomedes.fact: During the Achaean council held, Agamemnon asked for a volunteer to spy on the Trojans.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: The son of _____ explained "If another will go with me, I could do this in greater confidence and comfort
Diomedes.fact: The son of Tydeus explained "If another will go with me, I could do this in greater confidence and comfort.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: The hero instantly selected _____ for he was loved by Athena and was quick witted
Diomedes.fact: The hero instantly selected Odysseus for he was loved by Athena and was quick witted. Although Odysseus had deserted Diomedes in the battlefield that very day, instead of criticizing him, the latter praised his bravery in front of others.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Meanwhile, in a similar council held by _____, not a single prince or king would volunteer to spy on Achaeans
Diomedes.fact: Meanwhile, in a similar council held by Hector, not a single prince or king would volunteer to spy on Achaeans. Finally Hector managed to send Dolon, a good runner, after making a false oath (promising him Achilles' horses after the victory).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Finally Hector managed to send Dolon, a good runner, after making a false oath (promising him _____' horses after the victory)
Diomedes.fact: Finally Hector managed to send Dolon, a good runner, after making a false oath (promising him Achilles' horses after the victory).

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: The two kings lay among the corpses till _____ passed them and ran after him
Diomedes.fact: Finally Hector managed to send Dolon, a good runner, after making a false oath (promising him Achilles' horses after the victory). On their way to the Trojan camp, Diomedes and Odysseus discovered Dolon approaching the Achaean camp.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Dolon proved to be the better runner but _____ infused fresh strength into the son of Tydeus for she feared some other Achaean might earn the glory of being first to hit Dolon
Diomedes.fact: Dolon proved to be the better runner but Athena infused fresh strength into the son of Tydeus for she feared some other Achaean might earn the glory of being first to hit Dolon.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: According to Dolon, _____ and the other councilors were holding conference by the monument of great Ilus, away from the general tumult
Diomedes.fact: According to Dolon, Hector and the other councilors were holding conference by the monument of great Ilus, away from the general tumult. It is never explained in the epic why Dolon, specially mentioned as a man of lesser intelligence, came to notice this flaw while Hector (in spite of all his boasting) completely missed/ignored it.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: It is never explained in the epic why Dolon, specially mentioned as a man of lesser intelligence, came to notice this flaw while _____ (in spite of all his boasting) completely missed/ignored it
Diomedes.fact: According to Dolon, Hector and the other councilors were holding conference by the monument of great Ilus, away from the general tumult. It is never explained in the epic why Dolon, specially mentioned as a man of lesser intelligence, came to notice this flaw while Hector (in spite of all his boasting) completely missed/ignored it.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: In addition, he told about a major weakness in the _____ army
Diomedes.fact: In addition, he told about a major weakness in the Trojan army. Only the Trojans had watchfires; they, therefore, were awake and kept each other to their duty as sentinels; but the allies who have come from other places were asleep and left it to the Trojans to keep guard.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Having truthfully revealed valuable things, _____ expected to be taken as a prisoner to the ships, or to be tied up, while the other two found out whether he had told them the truth or not
Diomedes.fact: It is never explained in the epic why Dolon, specially mentioned as a man of lesser intelligence, came to notice this flaw while Hector (in spite of all his boasting) completely missed/ignored it. Rhesus was their king and Dolon described Rhesus' horses in this manner; "His horses are the finest and strongest that I have ever seen, they are whiter than snow and fleeter than any wind that blows".

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: If we set you free tonight, there is nothing to prevent your coming down once more to the _____ ships, either to play the spy or to meet us in open fight
Diomedes.fact: If we set you free tonight, there is nothing to prevent your coming down once more to the Achaean ships, either to play the spy or to meet us in open fight.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Although the original purpose of this night mission was spying on the _____, the information given by Dolon persuaded the two friends to plan an attack upon the Thracians
Diomedes.fact: Although the original purpose of this night mission was spying on the Trojans, the information given by Dolon persuaded the two friends to plan an attack upon the Thracians.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: They took the spoils and set them upon a tamarisk tree in honour of _____
Diomedes.fact: They took the spoils and set them upon a tamarisk tree in honour of Athena.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: Meanwhile, _____ gathered the team of Rhesus' horses
Diomedes.fact: Meanwhile, Odysseus gathered the team of Rhesus' horses.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: He was planning to kill more _____ and steal the chariot of the king with his armour when Athena advised him to retire, lest some other god might warn the Trojans
Diomedes.fact: He was planning to kill more Thracians and steal the chariot of the king with his armour when Athena advised him to retire, lest some other god might warn the Trojans.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: In Book XIII, _____ praises Meriones and claims the best warriors do in fact excel in both types of warfare, 'lokhos' (ambush) and 'polemos' (open battle)
Diomedes.fact: In Book XIII, Idomeneus praises Meriones and claims the best warriors do in fact excel in both types of warfare, 'lokhos' (ambush) and 'polemos' (open battle). Idomeneus' words portray ambush, "the place where the merit of men most shines through, where the coward and the resolute man are revealed", as a type of warfare only for the bravest.

Diomedes.subject: World Geography
Diomedes.question: The first night mission also fulfills one of the prophecies required for the fall of Troy: that Troy will not fall while the horses of _____ feed upon its plains
Diomedes.fact: The first night mission also fulfills one of the prophecies required for the fall of Troy: that Troy will not fall while the horses of Rhesus feed upon its plains. According to another version of the story, it had been foretold by an oracle that if the stallions of Rhesus were ever to drink from the river Scamander, which cuts across the Trojan plain, then the city of Troy would never fall.

Downhill creep.question: What is Downhill creep? Slow, downward progression of rock and soil down a low grade slope.
Downhill creep.fact: Downhill creep, also called soil creep or commonly just creep, is a type of creep characterized by the slow, downward progression of rock and soil down a low grade slope; it can also refer to slow deformation of such materials as a result of prolonged pressure and stress.

Drainage.subject: World Geography
Drainage.question: What is Drainage? Removal of water from an area of land.
Drainage.fact: Drainage is the natural or artificial removal of a surface's water and sub-surface water from an area with excess water.   The internal drainage of most agricultural soils can prevent severe waterlogging (anaerobic conditions that harm root growth), but many soils need artificial drainage to improve production or to manage water supplies.

Drainage basin.subject: World Geography
Drainage basin.question: What is Drainage basin? Land area where water converges to a common outlet.
Drainage basin.fact: A drainage basin is an area of land in which all flowing surface water converges to a single point, such as a river mouth, or flows into another body of water, such as a lake or ocean.

Drainage divide.subject: World Geography
Drainage divide.question: What is Drainage divide? Elevated terrain that separates neighbouring drainage basins.
Drainage divide.fact: A drainage divide, water divide, ridgeline, watershed, water parting or height of land is elevated terrain that separates neighboring drainage basins.

Drainage equation.subject: World Geography
Drainage equation.question: What is Drainage equation? Equation used in drainage design.
Drainage equation.fact: A drainage equation is an equation describing the relation between depth and spacing of parallel subsurface drains, depth of the watertable, depth and hydraulic conductivity of the soils.   A well known steady-state drainage equation is the Hooghoudt drain spacing equation.

Drainage research.question: What is Drainage research? Study of agricultural drainage systems.
Drainage research.fact: Drainage research is the study of agricultural drainage systems and their effects to arrive at optimal system design.   All these aspects can be subject of drainage research.

Drainage system (geomorphology).question: What is Drainage system (geomorphology)? Patterns formed by streams, rivers, and lakes in a drainage system.
Drainage system (geomorphology).fact: In geomorphology, drainage systems, also called river systems, are the patterns formed by the streams, rivers, and lakes in a particular drainage basin. Ecosystem.subject: World Geography
Ecosystem.question: The term was coined by _____, who came up with the word at Tansley's request
Ecosystem.fact: Ecosystem processes are known to "take place at a wide range of scales".  Therefore, the correct scale of study depends on the question asked.  === Origin and development of the term === The term "ecosystem" was first used in 1935 in a publication by British ecologist Arthur Tansley.  The term was coined by Arthur Roy Clapham, who came up with the word at Tansley's request.  Tansley devised the concept to draw attention to the importance of transfers of materials between organisms and their environment.  He later refined the term, describing it as "The whole system, .  including not only the organism-complex, but also the whole complex of physical factors forming what we call the environment"

Ecosystem.subject: World Geography
Ecosystem.question: The remainder, that portion of _____ that is not used up by respiration, is known as the net primary production (NPP)
Ecosystem.fact: Through the process of photosynthesis, plants capture energy from light and use it to combine carbon dioxide and water to produce carbohydrates and oxygen.  The photosynthesis carried out by all the plants in an ecosystem is called the gross primary production (GPP).  About half of the gross GPP is respired by plants in order to provide the energy that supports their growth and maintenance.  The remainder, that portion of GPP that is not used up by respiration, is known as the net primary production (NPP).  Total photosynthesis is limited by a range of environmental factors.  These include the amount of light available, the amount of leaf area a plant has to capture light (shading by other plants is a major limitation of photosynthesis), the rate at which carbon dioxide can be supplied to the chloroplasts to support photosynthesis, the availability of water, and the availability of suitable temperatures for carrying out photosynthesis.  === Energy flow === Energy and carbon enter ecosystems through photosynthesis, are incorporated into living tissue, transferred to other organisms that feed on the living and dead plant matter, and eventually released through respiration

Ecosystem.subject: World Geography
Ecosystem.question: The energetic cost is high for plants that support nitrogen-fixing symbionts—as much as _____ of gross primary production when measured in controlled conditions
Ecosystem.fact: Finally, there are also beneficial nutrients which may be required by certain plants or by plants under specific environmental conditions: aluminum, cobalt, iodine, nickel, selenium, silicon, sodium, vanadium.  Until modern times, nitrogen fixation was the major source of nitrogen for ecosystems.  Nitrogen-fixing bacteria either live symbiotically with plants or live freely in the soil.  The energetic cost is high for plants that support nitrogen-fixing symbionts—as much as 25% of gross primary production when measured in controlled conditions.  Many members of the legume plant family support nitrogen-fixing symbionts.  Some cyanobacteria are also capable of nitrogen fixation.  These are phototrophs, which carry out photosynthesis

Ecosystem.subject: World Geography
Ecosystem.question: Anthropogenic nitrogen inputs account for about _____ of all nitrogen fluxes in ecosystems
Ecosystem.fact: These are phototrophs, which carry out photosynthesis.  Like other nitrogen-fixing bacteria, they can either be free-living or have symbiotic relationships with plants.  Other sources of nitrogen include acid deposition produced through the combustion of fossil fuels, ammonia gas which evaporates from agricultural fields which have had fertilizers applied to them, and dust.  Anthropogenic nitrogen inputs account for about 80% of all nitrogen fluxes in ecosystems.  When plant tissues are shed or are eaten, the nitrogen in those tissues becomes available to animals and microbes.  Microbial decomposition releases nitrogen compounds from dead organic matter in the soil, where plants, fungi, and bacteria compete for it.  Some soil bacteria use organic nitrogen-containing compounds as a source of carbon, and release ammonium ions into the soil

Ecosystem.subject: World Geography
Ecosystem.question: It is intended to serve a similar role to the _____ on Climate Change
Ecosystem.fact: The report refers to natural systems as humanity's "life-support system", providing essential ecosystem services.  The assessment measures 24 ecosystem services and concludes that only four have shown improvement over the last 50 years, 15 are in serious decline, and five are in a precarious condition.  The Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) is an intergovernmental organization established to improve the interface between science and policy on issues of biodiversity and ecosystem services.  It is intended to serve a similar role to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.  Ecosystem services are limited and also threatened by human activities.  To help inform decision-makers, many ecosystem services are being assigned economic values, often based on the cost of replacement with anthropogenic alternatives.  The ongoing challenge of prescribing economic value to nature, for example through biodiversity banking, is prompting transdisciplinary shifts in how we recognize and manage the environment, social responsibility, business opportunities, and our future as a species

Ecosystem.subject: World Geography
Ecosystem.question: For example, the forests of eastern _____ still show legacies of cultivation which ceased in 1850 when large areas were reverted to forests
Ecosystem.fact: A drought, a colder than usual winter, and a pest outbreak all are short-term variability in environmental conditions.  Animal populations vary from year to year, building up during resource-rich periods and crashing as they overshoot their food supply.  Longer-term changes also shape ecosystem processes.  For example, the forests of eastern North America still show legacies of cultivation which ceased in 1850 when large areas were reverted to forests.  Another example is the methane production in eastern Siberian lakes that is controlled by organic matter which accumulated during the Pleistocene.  === Nutrient cycling === Ecosystems continually exchange energy and carbon with the wider environment.  Mineral nutrients, on the other hand, are mostly cycled back and forth between plants, animals, microbes and the soil

Ecosystem.subject: World Geography
Ecosystem.question: Long-term research at the site led to the discovery of acid rain in _____ in 1972
Ecosystem.fact: The Hubbard Brook Ecosystem Study started in 1963 to study the White Mountains in New Hampshire.  It was the first successful attempt to study an entire watershed as an ecosystem.  The study used stream chemistry as a means of monitoring ecosystem properties, and developed a detailed biogeochemical model of the ecosystem.  Long-term research at the site led to the discovery of acid rain in North America in 1972.  Researchers documented the depletion of soil cations (especially calcium) over the next several decades.  Ecosystems can be studied through a variety of approaches—theoretical studies, studies monitoring specific ecosystems over long periods of time, those that look at differences between ecosystems to elucidate how they work and direct manipulative experimentation.  Studies can be carried out at a variety of scales, ranging from whole-ecosystem studies to studying microcosms or mesocosms (simplified representations of ecosystems)
